newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse edges up,foreigners buy bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse edges up,foreigners buy bank shares.

text.p: Foreign investors dominated trade at the Nairobi Stock Exchange on Monday, lifting market sentiment in what otherwise would have been a dull trading session, brokers said.
The index edged up 2.70 points to close at 3530.43. Turnover was posted at 25.9 million shillings on 1,509,453 shares compared to 110.1 million shillings on 1,557,010 shares on Friday.
Foreigners traded Kenya Commercial Bank at between 110 and 114 from 110 and Firestone East Africa at 28.50 from 28.
"We've let it go up. It's is the only one climbing," a senior broker said referring to the commercial bank which traded at an all-time high of 125 on Friday on the special board.
They also traded 1.25 million shares of Kenya Airways at a reserve price of 9.50. On Friday the share closed at 8.25.
"No-one's really pessimistic about the market. The market will continue volatile. The way foreigners are buying is a clear indicator that we'll continue seeing such high turnovers," one broker said.
Brooke Bond was unchanged at 124 while Rea Vipingo edged to 9.30 from 9.20.
Uchumi Supermarket closed at 40 from 38.25 while Nation Printers & Publishers edged by a shilling to close at 116.
Kenya Power & Lighting closed at 171 from 172 while Total Kenya traded at 64.50 from 64.
